data.title: Apollo Cancels Planned $2 Billion Loan to Manchester City Parent After Premier League Ruling
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing people familiar with the matter, Apollo Global Management canceled plans to lend $2 billion to Manchester City parent City Football Group after an independent commission found the club had breached Premier League financial rules. Apollo had entered final loan negotiations but ended them after the commission announced its ruling in September this year.

The commission upheld 114 charges against Manchester City, finding that the club had overstated financial figures by more than £900 million from 2009 to 2018. It found that a private investment firm controlled by club owner Sheikh Mansour, a member of Abu Dhabi’s royal family, used sham commercial deals to cover part of some sponsors’ payments. Manchester City denies wrongdoing and plans to appeal. The appeal is expected to be heard in December; if it fails, penalties, including fines, points deductions or expulsion from the Premier League, could be imposed in 2027.

Filings at the UK’s Companies House show that Mansour injected £100 million of equity into City Football Group through an investment firm within a month of the ruling. Apollo’s proposed loan was intended to bolster the group’s liquidity and refinance existing credit. City Football Group owns clubs in Europe, the Americas and Asia.

Silver Lake holds a minority stake in City Football Group, investing $500 million in 2019 when the group was valued at $4.8 billion. Apollo, which manages more than $1 trillion in assets, has continued to expand its sports investments. Last year, it agreed to acquire a majority stake in Atletico Madrid at a valuation of more than €2 billion. In December 2024, it lent £80 million to Nottingham Forest, and in August this year it announced $2.6 billion in financing for the holding company of the New York Yankees.

data.title: Sanofi’s Next-Generation Rabies Vaccine Wins EU Approval for All Ages
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the European Commission has approved Sanofi’s VaxRabeo rabies vaccine for people of all ages, for both pre-exposure and post-exposure prevention. Sanofi announced the approval on November 19, marking the vaccine’s first marketing authorization anywhere in the world.

VaxRabeo uses Vero cell technology and is designed to reduce the risk of allergic reactions. Compared with Sanofi’s existing rabies vaccines, Verorab and Imovax Rabies, it has a shelf life of up to five years and can remain stable for 96 hours at temperatures up to 27°C before reconstitution.

The approval was based on comparative clinical studies covering all age groups and using pre-exposure and post-exposure vaccination schedules recommended by the World Health Organization. VaxRabeo produced protective antibody levels comparable to the existing vaccines and showed a good immune response to booster doses given 12 months after the initial vaccination or 24 to 36 months afterward.

The World Health Organization estimates that rabies is present in about 150 countries, causes about 59,000 deaths annually, and leads roughly 29 million people to receive post-exposure vaccination. The disease is mainly transmitted through the saliva of infected animals. Once symptoms appear, the fatality rate is nearly 100%, but timely vaccination can prevent the disease.

data.title: StoneX Analyst Says Gold Rebound From 13-Month Low Likely Reflects Short Covering
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing StoneX, spot gold rose 0.3% to $3,736 an ounce on Thursday after touching its lowest level in more than a year. StoneX Senior Market Analyst Matt Simpson said the rebound was more likely driven by short-covering than by fundamentals.

The Federal Reserve’s October meeting minutes showed markets assigning a 90% probability to a 25-basis-point rate hike in December.

data.title: STOCKS | Sony Outperforms Japanese Tech Shares, Rising Nearly 3% on GTA 6 Sales
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Sony shares rose nearly 3% to 4,363 yen on November 19, outperforming Japanese technology stocks. Data published by market research firm Sensor Tower showed that Take-Two’s GTA VI sold 17.07 million copies on its first day, with PlayStation accounting for 75% and Microsoft’s Xbox for the remaining 25%. Based on those figures, first-day sales were about 12.8 million copies on PlayStation and 4.27 million on Xbox.

The strong sales of GTA 6 are expected to significantly boost revenue from Sony’s game software business. More than 80% of PS5 consoles currently on the market are digital-only models, whose users need to buy and download games through the official PlayStation digital store. Sony receives a share of each game sale.

GTA 6 could also ease pressure from slowing PlayStation console sales. Sony previously raised console prices amid rising global memory and electronic-component costs, which affected hardware sales.

data.title: CoreWeave’s Three Founders Sell $3.3 Billion in Shares Since IPO; Cofounder Buys Company Bonds
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, CoreWeave co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Brian Venturo said on November 18 that he bought $30 million face value of the company’s unsecured bonds last week and plans to hold them until they mature on October 1, 2031. Venturo said the purchase was intended to signal his confidence in the company’s prospects.

Investors are closely watching CoreWeave’s debt-funded expansion and large share sales by company insiders. Regulatory filings show that the three co-founders have sold a combined $3.3 billion in shares since CoreWeave went public in March 2025, including $2.4 billion so far this year.

Venturo has sold more than $1.2 billion in shares since the IPO, including $734 million in the second quarter of this year. CEO Michael Intrator has sold more than $907 million so far this year, while co-founder Brannin McBee has sold about $1.06 billion in total.

CoreWeave has said the founders’ sales were made under prearranged trading plans, were fully disclosed and were routine. The three co-founders still own about 20% of the company combined.

data.title: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink Says Tighter U.S. AI Regulation Could Trigger Recession
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Nikkei and TV Tokyo, BlackRock CEO Larry Fink said in a joint interview in Tokyo on November 19 that stricter U.S. regulation of artificial intelligence could push the U.S. economy into recession and harm the global economy. Fink was in Japan for a board meeting. He estimated that U.S. investment demand related to AI stands at $7 trillion to $9 trillion and called for using capital markets to address a potential investment shortfall in AI development.

data.title: Deutsche Bank’s Italian Unit Concealed Losses of Up to €800 Million, Leaked Documents Show
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, leaked internal documents show that Deutsche Bank’s Italian unit concealed losses of up to about €800 million for more than a decade through derivatives trading and off-balance-sheet accounting, until an internal whistleblower brought the matter to light in 2018. Local management set up a secret reserve account called “tesoretto,” or “little treasure,” to cover shortfalls against profit targets.

The issue stemmed in part from a 2007 Italian legal reform allowing households to repay fixed-rate mortgages early without additional fees. The unit did not adjust its loan pricing or risk-management models accordingly and stopped sharing some loan data with group headquarters, leaving €2.8 billion in loans and €1.4 billion in early repayments out of headquarters’ records.

Deutsche Bank’s internal investigation, code-named Project Aetos, found €900 million in derivative positions without a sound economic basis. The unit also manipulated loan-loss provisions to build the secret reserve, which it used in 2011, 2014 and 2016 to meet profit targets. In 2020, the bank reported a €522 million financial loss to the European Central Bank; including unrealized losses, the potential total was €779 million. From 2018 to 2023, headquarters injected a total of €1 billion into the Italian unit.

The bank did not dismiss employees involved. Some departing executives received severance payments exceeding €1 million, and the bank waived its right to recover €5.25 million in deferred compensation. Former Italian unit head Flavio Valeri, who led it for 12 years, the local chief financial officer and the private banking head received written warnings for management failures, though the investigation found no individual misconduct. KPMG, which audited the unit, did not identify the issues while they were ongoing and later said financial statements did not need to be restated.

The findings also prompted questions about CEO Christian Sewing, who led an internal audit in 2014 that identified risk-management issues but whose recommended corrective measures were not implemented. Deutsche Bank said it had fully investigated the unit’s historical issues and appropriately informed relevant stakeholders. It said the matter had no material impact on the group or its business divisions, so no further group-level disclosure was required.

data.title: Record-Low U.S. Pending Home Sales Could Signal Relief for Bitcoin and Stocks
data.description: U.S. pending home sales fell 4.7% in October to 63.0, the lowest reading since records began in 2001. The decline may signal that mortgage rates have peaked and ease pressure on stocks and Bitcoin (BTC), according to BeInCrypto, although the Federal Reserve still expects further rate increases. Contract signings dropped 16.7% from a year earlier, with declines in all four U.S. regions. National Association of Realtors chief economist Lawrence Yun said October could mark the low point in this housing cycle as mortgage rates appear to have topped out. Freddie Mac’s 30-year mortgage rate eased to 7.11% by Nov. 12 after peaking at 7.40% in mid-October; mortgage rates had climbed 74 basis points from late August to early October, while the Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points in September. In November, the S&P 500 fell 3.4% and Bitcoin lost about 18%. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $2.8 billion in outflows so far this month. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 5.07% from 5.10% on Wednesday, while the two-year held at 4.80%. The Fed’s October meeting minutes showed almost all officials expected further increases, and Governor Christopher Waller said he favored a half-point December hike. The Dec. 8-9 meeting will test whether easing long-term yields support Yun’s view or further rate increases renew pressure on risk assets.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Amber Group to Focus More on AI Investment and Incubation, Adjust Trading and Market-Making Operations
data.description: Amber Group said it is placing greater emphasis on AI-related investment and incubation while adjusting the scale and capital allocated to its market-making and trading businesses. According to Foresight News, the company sees significant long-term opportunities in AI and is shifting more of its business and resources to the sector. The changes will affect some team members, whom Amber Group said it will support through the transition. The company added that its businesses are continuing to operate.

data.title: AI TRENDS | South Korea's Financial Regulator Asks Financial Companies to Report AI Exposure
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service has asked major domestic financial companies to disclose their exposure to the artificial intelligence industry. Choi Beom-jeon, head of the agency's financial industry supervision group, said the regulator is assessing exposure as a precaution amid growing concerns about hyperscale data centers and AI companies. The first-of-its-kind survey covers large firms, including banks, brokerages and insurers, and asks about direct or indirect investments in AI companies and direct lending relationships; some firms have already submitted questionnaires.

The assessment aims to gauge South Korean companies' vulnerabilities in the AI sector. South Korea is viewed as a bellwether for the regional AI boom, while global scrutiny of the technology is increasing. AI has attracted hundreds of billions of dollars in investment, most of it debt-financed.
